title: Feedback factory: multiple faint radio jets detected in a cluster at z = 2
question: What is the role of AGN radio-jet based kinetic feedback and the compliance of cluster galaxies to the TIR-radio correlation within the z=2 galaxy cluster CL J1449+0856?

what.value: ALMA CO[4-3] and CO[3-2] line fluxes, 870 \mu m continuum fluxes and image, star formation rates, and stellar masses of cluster galaxies

evidence.quote: The corresponding flux measurements along with resulting star formation rates (SFR) and stellar mass
We borrow their results from the spectral line flux extraction of CO\[4-3\] and CO\[3-2\] along with the continuum flux measurements at 870 $\mu$m obtained for each of the cluster galaxies

what.value: ALMA+ACA 92 GHz Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect 5\sigma signal and residual map

evidence.quote: Furthermore, ALMA+ACA data of CL J1449+0856 at 92 GHz was presented in (cite: gobat19) in cycle 4 (Project ID: 2016.1.01107, PI: R. Gobat).
We here make use of their results, including the Sunyaev-Zel’dovich effect (SZ) 5\sigma signal and the corresponding residual map.

what.value: Diffuse X-ray ICM luminosity (7.2 x 10^43 ergs s^-1) and instantaneous energy injection rate from SFR and AGN outflows (~5 x 10^44 ergs s^-1)

evidence.loc: Radio emission: How much do we really have?
evidence.quote: Finally, with the additional information of the X-ray luminosity (7.2 ~ \times 10^{43} ~ergs~ s^{-1}) at 0.1–2.4 keV from the ICM of CL J1449+0856 (cite: gobat11; valentino16), we place this cluster among the other galaxy clusters from the (cite: mittal09) HIFLUGCS sample in Fig. 1.
This power is \sim 0.25 times the already estimated energy injection rate calculated by (cite: valentino16) from SFR and AGN outflows (\sim 5~\times 10^{44} ~ergs~ s^{-1}).

what.value: Low-redshift HIFLUGCS cluster sample radio and X-ray luminosity measurements for comparison

evidence.loc: Radio emission: How much do we really have?
evidence.quote: Since we are also aiming to investigate the differences in the mode of operation of radio-jets at higher redshifts compared to their low redshift counterparts, we make a comparison to the results presented in (cite: mittal09).

what.value: q_TIR vs M_* relation for main-sequence star-forming galaxies

evidence.quote: We also add to this the results from (cite: delvecchio20), which is a follow-up study of Main-Sequence star-forming galaxies from (cite: delvecchio17) but for an M_{*}-selected sample from the VLA-COSMOS 3 GHz survey (cite: smolcic17).

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image JVLA 3 GHz and GMRT 325 MHz radio continuum data
recipe.method: Calibrate, flag RFI, and image JVLA S-band (A and C configurations) and GMRT P-band data using TCLEAN in CASA, with self-calibration applied to GMRT data
key_parameters: JVLA A-config: Briggs robust = 2.0, nterms = 2, wprojplanes = 128, multiscale scales = [2, 5, 10] pixels; JVLA C-config and GMRT: Briggs robust = 0.5

recipe.goal: Measure 3 GHz radio continuum fluxes and point-source sensitivity via PSF fitting
recipe.method: Inject ~200 artificial point sources with GALFIT to determine 1-sigma sensitivity, then iteratively fit and subtract point sources at HST/WFC3 and ALMA 870 um prior positions followed by free-position point sources for residual jet components
key_parameters: Artificial source flux range: 4.5 - 7.5 \mu Jy within 80'' radius; exclusion radius 1'' around >4\sigma pixels
assumptions: Sources are unresolved point sources smaller than the synthesized beam HPBW

recipe.goal: Compute TIR-radio luminosity ratio (q_TIR) and compare with the main-sequence relation
recipe.method: Convert 3 GHz flux to rest-frame 1.4 GHz luminosity and combine with L_IR (derived from ALMA 870 \mu m fluxes) to calculate q_TIR for cluster galaxies and 3\sigma upper limits for jet sources
assumptions: Radio spectral index \alpha = -0.7 for star formation; cosmology \Omega_m = 0.3, \Omega_\Lambda = 0.7, H_0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1; Chabrier IMF

recipe.goal: Test physical origin of the counterpart-less radio sources via SED prediction and multi-wavelength image stacking
recipe.method: Calculate noise fluctuation probabilities, predict expected 870 \mu m fluxes assuming star formation, and median stack 1.5'' cutouts of the ALMA 870 \mu m continuum image and HST F140W image at the radio source positions
key_parameters: 1.5'' cutout size for ALMA 870 \mu m median stacking; 20'' radius (170 kpc) region for noise probability calculation
assumptions: Spectral index \alpha = -0.7 and Bethermin et al. (2012) main-sequence SED templates

recipe.goal: Calculate integrated radio-jet luminosity, mechanical cavity power, SZ residual correlation, and Inverse-Compton X-ray contribution
recipe.method: Integrate rest-frame 10 MHz - 10 GHz radio luminosity from the 6 jets, convert to cavity power P_cav via the O'Sullivan et al. (2011) scaling relation, compare jet locations with the ALMA+ACA 92 GHz SZ residual map, and estimate IC X-ray flux limits from GMRT 325 MHz and Chandra stacking
assumptions: Jet spectral index \alpha = -1.04 \pm 0.03 (explored range -0.7 to -1.5, and -1.2); cavity energy E_cav = 4pV; Lorentz factor 10^3 - 10^5 and photon index 2 for IC calculation

answer_key.quantity: JVLA 3 GHz A-configuration RMS noise / point-source sensitivity

evidence.quote: The primary beam FWHM of the 3 GHz observations was 15’, and the FWHM of the synthesised beam at this wavelength was \sim0.83^{\prime\prime}\times0.67^{\prime\prime} at PA = -4.17° for the A-configuration data, with an RMS noise of 1.34\mu Jy/beam over an effective bandwidth of 1.5 GHz.
The final synthesised beam was \sim 7.4^{\prime\prime} \times 6.6^{\prime\prime} at PA = 7.8° and the RMS noise of the resulting image was 92 \mu Jy/beam.

answer_key.quantity: Total 3 GHz flux from the 6 detected radio-jets

evidence.quote: We measure a total flux of 30.6 \pm 3.3~\mu Jy from the 6 detected jets.

evidence.loc: Radio emission: How much do we really have?
evidence.quote: To make a comparison, we add up the contributions of all the detected jets in place of the jets from a central AGN, which gives us a flux of 30.6\pm3.3 \, \mu Jy and a corresponding integrated radio luminosity (10 MHz–10 GHz rest-frame) of 2.1 ~(\pm 0.2)~ \times 10^{41} ~ergs~ s^{-1}.

Pre-reduced ALMA 870 um continuum image from Coogan et al. (2018) and 92 GHz SZ residual map from Gobat et al. (2019), as ALMA reduction parameters are not restated in this paper
missing_for_reproduction: Manual flagging tables and iterative self-calibration parameters for JVLA 12A-188 and GMRT 23_068
Exact manual clean masks used during incremental TCLEAN runs for JVLA A and C configurations
Reduced ALMA 870 um continuum map (from Coogan et al. 2018), ALMA+ACA 92 GHz SZ residual map (from Gobat et al. 2019), HST/WFC3 F140W mosaic, and Chandra X-ray event files
SED fitting code or look-up tables from Bethermin et al. (2012, 2015) used to map 3 GHz and 870 um fluxes to L_IR
score_reason: Raw VLA, GMRT, and ALMA project codes are public and the JVLA TCLEAN and GALFIT source-extraction parameters are well-specified, along with explicit equations and coordinates/fluxes for all targets and jets; however, manual RFI flagging/masking in VLA/GMRT reduction and reliance on pre-reduced ALMA, HST, and Chandra maps from earlier papers prevent fully automated end-to-end reproduction.
rediscovery_reason: All raw radio and ALMA datasets are public, the core scientific results are concrete numeric flux and power measurements of discrete sources with published coordinates, and the VLA re-imaging + GALFIT point-source extraction + ALMA 870 um non-detection check is a well-defined recipe.
